title: The 8237A DMA controller, its registers
covers: The registers of the 8237A DMA controller: channel registers, command, status, request, mask, mode and the software commands

rows.text: Each channel has a 16-bit Current Address register that holds the address used during DMA transfers.
The address is incremented or decremented automatically after each transfer, and its intermediate values are stored in the register.
The microprocessor writes and reads the Current Address register in successive 8-bit bytes.
An Autoinitialize may reinitialize the Current Address register to its original value, and only after an EOP.
Each channel has a 16-bit Current Word Count register that determines the number of transfers to be performed.
The actual number of transfers is one more than the programmed count: a count of 100 gives 101 transfers.
The word count is decremented after each transfer, its intermediate value is stored in the register, and going from zero to FFFFH generates a TC.
The microprocessor loads and reads the Current Word Count register in successive 8-bit bytes in the Program Condition.
Without Autoinitialize the Current Word Count register has the count FFFFH after TC; Autoinitialize can occur only when an EOP occurs.
Each channel has 16-bit Base Address and Base Word Count registers that store the original values of the current registers, restored during Autoinitialize.
The base registers are written simultaneously with their corresponding current registers, in 8-bit bytes in the Program Condition.
The base registers cannot be read by the microprocessor.
A3 = 0, A0 = 0: a write loads the base and current address of channel A2 A1, low byte at flip-flop 0, high byte at 1.
A3 = 0, A0 = 0: a read returns the current address of channel A2 A1, low byte at flip-flop 0, high byte at 1.
A3 = 0, A0 = 1: a write loads the base and current word count of channel A2 A1, low byte at flip-flop 0, high byte at 1.
A3 = 0, A0 = 1: a read returns the current word count of channel A2 A1, low byte at flip-flop 0, high byte at 1.
A write or a read picks the low or high address byte by m_msb, then toggles it; a read with side effects disabled does not toggle it.
A read of an address or word count register first calls DoCallBack on the channel with DMA_READ_COUNTER.
A write or a read picks the low or high count byte by m_msb, then toggles it; a read with side effects disabled does not toggle it.

rows.text: The Status register can be read out by the microprocessor; it tells which channels reached a terminal count and which have pending DMA requests.
With A3 = 1, A2 A1 A0 = 0 and IOR low, a read returns the Status register.
Bits 0 to 3 are set every time a TC is reached by that channel or an external EOP is applied.
Bits 0 to 3 are cleared on each Status Read.
Bits 0 to 3 are cleared upon Reset.
Bits 4 to 7 are set whenever their corresponding channel is requesting service.
A Status read clears bits 0 to 3 with m_status &= 0xf0, but not when side effects are disabled.
When bit 0x40 of the command register is set, a Status read returns bits 4 to 7 inverted.

rows.text: The Command register is 8 bits wide and controls the operation of the 8237A.
The microprocessor programs the Command register in the Program Condition.
The Command register is cleared by Reset or a Master Clear instruction.
With A3 = 1, A2 A1 A0 = 0 and IOW low, a write loads the Command register.
A write at offset 0x08 does nothing: its case body is only a break, with a comment that the command register is not used.
The 8237A can respond to requests for DMA service initiated by software as well as by a DREQ.
Each channel has a request bit in the 4-bit Request register; the bits are non-maskable and subject to the priority encoder.
Each Request register bit is set or reset separately under software control.
A request bit is cleared upon generation of a TC or an external EOP.
The entire Request register is cleared by a Reset.
A write at A3 = 1, A2 A1 = 0, A0 = 1 with IOW low loads the Request register, in the proper form of data word.
To make a software request, the channel must be in Block Mode.
A write at offset 0x09 sets or clears no request bit: its case body holds only a comment and a break.
A write at offset 0x09 loads nothing: its case body holds only a comment and a break.
Each channel has a mask bit that, when set, disables the incoming DREQ.
Each mask bit is set when its associated channel produces an EOP, if the channel is not programmed for Autoinitialize.
Each bit of the 4-bit Mask register may be set or cleared separately under software control.
The Mask register is also set by a Reset, which disables all DMA requests until a clear Mask register instruction allows them.
The instruction that sets or clears one mask bit is similar in form to the one used with the Request register.
A write at A3 = 1, A2 = 0, A1 = 1, A0 = 0 with IOW low sets or clears one mask bit.
A write also records the guest as the actor that masked the channel, in masked_by, before calling SetMask.
Each channel has a 6-bit Mode register.
When the microprocessor writes the Mode register in the Program Condition, bits 0 and 1 select which channel Mode register is written.
A write at A3 = 1, A2 = 0, A1 = 1, A0 = 1 with IOW low writes the Mode register of one channel.
A Mode write also clears the written channel's TC bit in the Status register.
A Mode write stores bits 2 to 5 as autoinit, direction and transfer type; its case body stores nothing from bits 6 and 7.
An internal flip-flop gives one more address bit, which selects the upper or lower byte of the 16-bit Address and Word Count registers.
The flip-flop is reset by Master Clear or Reset.
A separate software command can also reset this flip-flop.
Special software commands are decoded as sets of addresses with CS and IOW and do not use the data bus; they include Clear First/Last Flip-Flop and Master Clear.
The software commands do not depend on any specific bit pattern on the data bus.
Clear First/Last Flip-Flop must be executed before writing or reading new address or word count information, to start from a known state.
With A3 A2 A1 A0 = 1100 and IOW low, a write executes Clear Byte Pointer Flip/Flop.
Master Clear has the same effect as the hardware Reset.
Master Clear clears the Command, Request and Temporary registers and the internal first/last flip-flop.
Master Clear clears the Status register.
Master Clear sets the Mask register.
After Master Clear the 8237A enters the Idle cycle.
With A3 A2 A1 A0 = 1101 and IOW low, a write executes Master Clear.
Master Clear executes m_status &= 0xf0, which clears bits 0 to 3 of Status and keeps bits 4 to 7.
Master Clear also sets the last served channel to 3 and calls set_hreq(0), set_eop(CLEAR_LINE) and set_dack.
Master Clear clears the flip-flop; the case body stores no Command, Request or Temporary register.
Master Clear clears the tcount flag of each channel, which Status read reports as bits 0 to 3; the case writes no request flag.
Master Clear enters no Idle cycle: the case body only masks channels and clears tcount and flipflop.
The Temporary register holds data during memory-to-memory transfers.
After the transfers the microprocessor can read the last word moved, in the Program Condition.
The Temporary register always contains the last byte transferred in the previous memory-to-memory operation, unless cleared by a Reset.
With A3 A2 A1 A0 = 1101 and IOR low, a read returns the Temporary register.
A read at offset 0x0D reaches the default arm of the switch: it logs an undefined DMA port and returns 0xffffffff.

rows.text: Clearing the mask bits of all four channels enables them to accept DMA requests.
The Clear Mask Register command clears the mask bits of all four channels.
With A3 A2 A1 A0 = 1110 and IOW low, a write executes Clear Mask Register.
Each channel is also marked as masked by the guest, in masked_by, before SetMask clears its mask.
All four bits of the Mask register may also be written with a single command.
With A3 A2 A1 A0 = 1111 and IOW low, a write loads all four Mask register bits.
Each channel is also marked as masked by the guest, in masked_by, before SetMask takes its bit from the value.
In Figure 6 the combinations with IOR low at offsets 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B and 0x0C are marked Illegal.
A read at offset 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B or 0x0C is Illegal.
A read at offsets 0x09 to 0x0C returns data, which starts at 0, because the switch has no case for these offsets.
A read at offsets 0x09 to 0x0B takes the default arm, logs an undefined DMA port and returns 0xffffffff; a read at 0x0C also clears the flip-flop.

A read at offset 0x0E or 0x0F is Illegal.
